items.title: David Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2022
items.q: If you listen to Kamasi Washington’s first record and hear all those voices and stuff that’s right off Billy Harper’s first record.

ctx.x: And with Kamasi Washington you’re like I mean here’s the living embodiment of everything he’s trying to do. If you listen to Kamasi Washington’s first record and hear all those voices and stuff that’s right off Billy Harper’s first record. You know. It’s Billy Harper, Pharaoh Sanders and a little of Coltrane. I mean you know be brought back 70s spiritual jazz to a new generation and more power to him for that, but at least be curious enough to check out Billy Harper. I mean Kamasi did it himself, he did a gig…

like hey I’ve got a new record out. You know? Or they want to talk about his chop problem or — hey, this is a positive day, I found a way to make a record anyway and I think it’s pretty good and don’t you want to talk about it? And after a while I said like, after a day of interviews he was like oh God. So I really think the mentality is isn’t it great that this dead person is still alive to tell us about all this stuff.
